title: Invert a Dictionary
hints: Iterating a dictionary gives `(key, value)` pairs.
Append each student to the list for their grade using `default: []`, then sort every list.
jsBridge: JS: `Object.entries(g).reduce(...)`. Swift iterates `(key, value)` tuples directly with `for (k, v) in dict`, and `dict.keys.sorted()` gives order. Plain dictionary iteration order is arbitrary and changes between runs.

`Dictionary(grouping:by:)` vs `reduce(into:)` with `[k, default: []].append(v)`: which one builds fewer intermediate arrays?
Why must a test assert on sorted keys, or compare dictionaries with `==`, rather than printing a dictionary?
